Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fmri.pipeline 0.4-1

MEDuSA learning sequence and workflow documentation

  • Add conceptual and executable workflow vignettes covering cross-run HRF learning, noise scaling, operator-based epoch de-mixing, duration models, NIfTI inputs, and the handoff to multilevel analysis.
  • Revise the technical companion through PR #54, align descriptions with the current implementation, distinguish legacy benchmark tables from live experiments, and remove unsupported forecasts of human-data gains.

Banded linear deconvolution solver and exact Takahashi trace

  • deconvolve_reglin_cpp() now exploits the strict banded structure of Hk⊤Hk+λP+δIH_k^\top H_k + \lambda P + \delta I (half-bandwidth b=max⁡(kernel_len−1+𝕀(prewhiten),bP)b = \max(\text{kernel\_len} - 1 + \mathbb{I}(\text{prewhiten}), \; b_P)), replacing dense O(nlatent3)O(n_{\text{latent}}^3) normal-equation solves and dense matrix-RHS trace evaluations with an in-place O(nlatentb2)O(n_{\text{latent}} b^2) lower-banded Cholesky factorization, contiguous multi-signal forward/backward substitution, and the exact O(nlatentb2)O(n_{\text{latent}} b^2) Takahashi banded-inverse recursion for effective degrees of freedom tr⁡(A(λ)−1Hk⊤Hk)\operatorname{tr}(A(\lambda)^{-1} H_k^\top H_k).
  • hrf_inverse_operator_cpp(), hrf_score_run_cpp(), and hrf_noise_profile_cpp() now eliminate dense m×mm \times m AR(1) whitening matrix construction and dense O(m2L)O(m^2 L) / O(Lmm0)O(L m m_0) matrix multiplications in favor of in-place column-wise bidiagonal whitening, tridiagonal W⊤WW^\top W stencil accumulation, L1-tiled banded Cholesky solves (for nuisance_mode = "ignore"), and single-pass batch normalization across the REML noise grid.

Coefficient recovery validation

  • Test fixed window-sum and calibrated-template amplitude readouts, and regression through the frozen inverse’s transformed event design. Include active/confounded nulls, off-library HRFs, matched references and a direct forward GLS benchmark. See COEFFICIENT_RECOVERY_VALIDATION.md. These are validation candidates; package algorithms and defaults are unchanged.

Parametric recovery validation

  • Add a separate simulation study with genuine neural trial variability, task-active RPE nulls, correlated task confounds, and paired true-HRF, true-covariance, noiseless and matched-grid references. Audit coefficient bias, coverage, false positives and power across runs and independent datasets at eight fixed lambdas. Native inverse operators and trial regression factorizations are reused. See PARAMETRIC_RECOVERY_VALIDATION.md.

Noise-aware HRF evidence and event recovery diagnostics

  • Cross-run HRF fitting now defaults to pooled grid-REML AR(1) covariance, conditional GLS task/shape evidence with library corrections, training-run compatibility, and a fixed penalty toward the prespecified shape. Unsupported adaptation has an explicit parcel/prespecified fallback. Tests are conditional on the noise/mean model and are not whole-brain significance or posterior confidence. noise_model = "ols", evidence = "legacy" retains the prior fit.
  • The native inverse shares operators across HRF/noise strata and uses original acquisition times across censor gaps. AR/calibrated fits use observation masks during scaling and fitting by default. Nuisance adjustment remains explicit; optional joint projection applies to both convolution and observations. Unidentifiable covariance is reported rather than silently assumed white.
  • diagnose_crossrun_recovery() reports conditional event amplitude gain and excess leakage relative to the ideal readout, accounting for natural neural window overlap, fractional onsets, masks, and the frozen inverse. It does not automatically rescale amplitudes. See NOISE_AWARE_HRF_RECOVERY.md for review, independent reference checks, repeated validation, and throughput benchmarks.

Cross-run HRF estimation and spatial regularization

  • hrf_library() constructs a small unit-sum HRF library. estimate_crossrun_hrf() selects HRFs using other runs only, with batched Rcpp/BLAS training fits, nuisance regressors, observation masks, explicit support gates, and a recorded parcel/prespecified fallback hierarchy. Training can use condition means or free event amplitudes for signed trial responses that would otherwise average away, without supplying RPE values.
  • Explicit parcel pooling and optional voxel shape penalties toward training-derived parcel HRFs provide spatial regularization. These constrain HRF selection without spatially smoothing recovered neural activity. Strength and effect-size thresholds are user-controlled. The original heuristic mode does not supply significance tests.
  • deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() applies frozen HRFs with required fixed lambda, grouped inverse operators, bounded caching, block multiplication, and recorded per-voxel scaling. Existing NIfTI/file deconvolution defaults are unchanged. See CROSSRUN_HRF_GUIDE.md and the reproducible review/benchmark scripts.
  • HRF_ESTIMATION_VALIDATION.md reports 480 independent simulated datasets comparing learned, canonical, and true HRFs at three fixed inverse penalties. Learning helps with stable shape mismatch but can hurt with low SNR, zero-mean signed responses, run changes, or neural-duration mismatch. The original support gate accepted all null free-event fits under colored noise; support labels are not confidence measures. Estimator settings were not tuned to these results. Reproducible scripts, compact tables, and figures are included.

Auditable event overlap and impulse recovery

  • Alignment now interpolates within each unit’s valid acquisition segments before aggregation. Explicit invalid values/masks block interpolation, and brackets wider than the acquisition TR are missing by default. Off-grid median/SD now summarize interpolated units; means with changing contributors also change.
  • overlap_policy supports allow, legacy truncate, and whole-window exclude. NULL retains collision-column truncation when explicitly configured, otherwise allows overlap. valid_col, neighbor_events, and max_gap pass through file and batch alignment settings. No policy claims physiological isolation.
  • Outputs report per-lag contributor/reason counts, acquisition-time IDs and epoch reuse, neighboring events, simultaneous events, window overlap, and run edges. Source clocks are returned as attributes; file alignment adds alignment_file and writes a .sources.csv clock sidecar beside requested outputs.
  • deconvolution_impulse_diagnostics() evaluates isolated impulses on actual event schedules under frozen linear settings, including specified HRF mismatch, centering, whitening and padding. Recovery and source-to-target window metrics are conditional diagnostics, not measured neural-attribution fractions.
  • EVENT_ALIGNMENT_OVERLAP_GUIDE.md documents changed semantics, limitations, review checks, and the runnable inst/examples/event_overlap_review.R example. Regenerate existing alignment outputs to adopt the new behavior.

Deconvolution scaling, Wiener tuning, and performance

  • Linear deconvolution supports explicit scaling = "zscore", "demean", "none", or "psc"; z-scoring remains the default. Legacy normalization flags still work. Voxelwise settings now control the actual preprocessing, applied once before padding. Bush voxelwise fits require z-scored input.
  • Per-voxel .scaling.csv sidecars record the applied centers and divisors; file metadata records scaling, algorithm, and units. Original-series files expose BOLD_input, with BOLD_z retained only for z-scored observations. Regenerate existing outputs to adopt these changes.
  • Bush resampling uses the same normalized observations for its base fit and residual construction. Its new normalize argument defaults to TRUE; voxelwise callers disable redundant normalization. The voxelwise Bush 2015 path now forwards beta and retains matrix dimensions for single-voxel fits.
  • Scalar Wiener GCV uses the exact finite-observation smoother trace rather than summing padded Fourier gains. Adaptive PSD Wiener requires fixed lambda and HRF; its conditional filter trace is labeled and GCV is missing, avoiding invalid automatic selection from a data-dependent filter.
  • The C++ linear solver builds difference-penalty crossproducts directly and skips scoring for fixed-parameter matrix-only fits. Wiener fitting reuses input/kernel FFTs across candidates and skips unrequested fixed-parameter scoring. The R reference implementation remains available for numerical comparisons.

Event alignment and file identity

  • Missing/nonfinite event onsets and unsupported windows retain explicit missing epochs with epoch_status; nonfinite collision times no longer abort runs. Original event variable mappings are preserved during alignment.
  • Zero-width, one-sided, and sub-sample windows use a unique grid within the requested bounds. An exact singleton observation can be retained without interpolation; duplicate reshape keys cannot silently turn signals into counts.
  • Default deconvolution names are visible, and each new output has an identity metadata sidecar. Alignment supports explicit file manifests, alphanumeric IDs, sessions, and leading-zero labels, with legacy filenames as a fallback. Discovery includes old hidden outputs and excludes sidecars.
  • Alignment records a status for every input file and stops on failures by default. Explicit fail_on_error = FALSE permits partial output with a warning. Status is returned in file_status and saved beside requested CSV outputs.

Voxelwise deconvolution correctness

  • Replaced 3dmaskdump with internal RNifti/Rcpp extraction using the same masked voxel indices as the output metadata. Atlas, additional mask, and input spatial geometry are validated before extraction. afni_dir remains accepted for compatibility but is ignored.
  • Constant and nonfinite signals are excluded before scaling and fitting, so they cannot invalidate other voxels or influence global tuning. Output rows and columns are preserved with missing estimates and explicit status values (decon_status in voxelwise output, signal_status in linear diagnostics).

Confound cache invalidation and batch exit status

  • Confound caches now record settings, demeaning, run inputs, and source-file fingerprints. Changes rebuild confounds, column metadata, exclusion decisions, and truncation data together, including cached raw confound and motion inputs. Original image provenance prevents repeated volume dropping when finalized run data are reused. Legacy caches rebuild from original inputs; a previously truncated run without provenance requires its original image and volume count. Existing fitted models must still be explicitly re-estimated after changes.

  • Generated batch scripts now retain nonzero task exit statuses in both serial and background execution, wait for every background task, and preserve failures through cleanup. Each task runs in its own subshell with set -e; setup and cleanup failures also produce a nonzero status. Standard shell rules for conditionals and pipelines still apply. ## L2 model refitting and concatenated confounds

  • L2 refits now preserve configured covariate transformations and factor reference levels. Transformation parameters are recomputed from complete retained runs within each subject/session or pooled subject, according to the L2 scope.

  • Concatenated L1 confounds now keep each session/run’s spike regressors separate, with zeros outside that run. Single-spike regressors retain their matrix shape and column names so they are correctly identified during concatenation.

  • Existing analyses need regenerated per-run confounds (including column metadata), concatenated confounds, and L2 designs, followed by re-estimation of affected models.

Declarative FWE correction workflow

  • Added a serializable fwe_spec() API for describing level-3 FWE corrections with semantic model/contrast selectors, method options, correction masks, and scheduler settings. Specifications can be read from and written to YAML.

  • Added pTFCE plan and execution support through plan_fwe_correction(), run_fwe_plan(), and refresh_fwe_plan(). A single specification can fan out across all selected level-3 z-statistic maps, with explicit preflight status for required inputs and optional dry-run command inspection.

  • Added persistent FWE result snapshots and artifact manifests via collect_fwe_results() and fwe_result_artifacts(), providing stable, semantically selectable output paths for downstream analyses.

ROI extraction and scheduler error handling

  • ROI extraction now validates every statistic image against the mask’s spatial dimensions, voxel sizes, units, and transform before indexing. Misaligned inputs stop extraction with a resampling/registration diagnostic. Reported coordinates use the same sform-first transform as the geometry checks.
  • Completed L3 ROI extraction using the shared group-output lookup, preserving lower-level contrast identities and pooled/per-session metadata without duplicating maps for each subject. Group-only extraction no longer requires lower-level setup tables, and L1-to-L3 analyses are supported.
  • Slurm cancellations, including CANCELLED by <uid> responses, are terminal failures in wait_for_job(). Failed submissions with fail_on_error = FALSE warn and return NULL without attempting to track a nonexistent job.
  • Removed the redundant package reload from test setup and added package-local command guards so unit tests fail on unmocked scheduler submissions.

Bug fixes in build_design_matrix / fmri.stimulus convolution

  • Fix: overlapping events silently overwritten during stimulus construction. construct_stimulus (inside fmri.stimulus) used assignment (stim[idx] <- values[i]) when building the microtime stimulus vector. When two events overlapped in time (e.g., long-duration events with short ITIs), later events overwrote earlier ones, silently producing incorrect regressors. Fixed to use additive accumulation (stim[idx] <- stim[idx] + values[i]), which is correct by linearity of convolution. This affected all normalization modes (none, durmax_1, evtmax_1).

  • Fix: microtime bin truncation causing position-dependent convolution peaks. Floating-point arithmetic in fmri.stimulus when converting onset times to microtime bins could produce values like 2013.999... instead of 2014, which R then truncated to the wrong bin. This shifted events by one microtime step, causing identical events at different run positions to have ~0.4% different peak amplitudes. Fixed by applying round() to microtime onset and duration indices.

  • Optimized evtmax_1 normalization. Replaced the previous approach of N separate full-run FFT convolutions (one per event) with precomputed HRF peaks via small padded windows, followed by a single combined convolution. This also eliminates the previous fragile workaround for end-of-run events (re-convolving at the center of the run to estimate the “true” peak). Speedups of 2-9x depending on number of events, number of unique durations, and run length.

  • Thread microtime_resolution parameter through convolve_regressor to ensure peak lookups and grid-phase computation always use the same resolution as the main convolution.

  • Fix: insufficient convolution padding with sub-second TRs. convolve_stimulus used a fixed 20-TR padding for edge-effect suppression, which at TR=0.5s was only 10 seconds — not enough for the double-gamma HRF undershoot to decay (still ~-0.02 at 20s). Changed to 30 seconds of absolute time padding regardless of TR, preventing circular convolution artifacts near run boundaries in multiband acquisitions.

Repeated timing rows and within-trial occurrences

  • Fixed L1 setup for occurrence-keyed signals when subject events are aggregated as a data.table. The occurrence validation added in July used data-frame column-selection syntax that data.table interpreted as a request for a literal join_cols column, causing every affected design build to fail and leaving an empty FSL setup table.

  • run_feat_sepjobs() now validates its FSL setup table before model filtering and reports a clear upstream-setup diagnostic instead of the misleading object 'l1_model' not found error.

  • Pipeline inputs and time-series multipliers now copy incoming data.tables to ordinary data.frames only when necessary. Fresh rbindlist() aggregations are likewise normalized at data-frame API boundaries without copying caller-owned objects or converting existing data.frames.

  • mixed_by() and fill_atlas_with_stats() now isolate their internal data.table operations from caller-owned inputs. Keying, sorting, and conversion inside these functions no longer change an input object’s class, key, or row order by reference.

  • trial_data now supports ragged timing rows: a row may contain trial-level timings alongside a within-trial occurrence, and sparse onset columns use NA to indicate no occurrence on that row. Trial identifiers may be NA for free-running occurrences.

  • Exact duplicate timing/value records are collapsed before convolution to prevent copied trial rows from inflating regressors. Set keep_duplicate_occurrences: true on a YAML signal to retain them.

  • Parametric modulators and within-subject factors now align to an internal timing-occurrence key, rather than run_number + trial, so repeated trials do not create many-to-many joins. Modulator values must be present on each modeled timing row; missing values omit that occurrence.

  • Beta-series signals now require exactly one distinct timing occurrence per trial after duplicate collapse and reject missing trial identifiers or ambiguous multi-occurrence trials.

  • Removed unused subtrial classes, mappings, arguments, and documentation.

Backend system overhaul

  • Per-level and per-model backend selection via gpa$level_backends, execution_backend, and producer_backend fields
  • Artifact-based dependency resolution: backends now declare which artifacts they produce and require, and the pipeline validates these at submission time
  • Preflight report logged at pipeline start showing resolved backends, producer mappings, and artifact satisfaction for each analysis level
  • harvest_l3_inputs() replaces the former harvest_fsl_copes() with a dispatcher that routes to backend-specific harvesters based on the declared producer_backend
  • Run-time backend overrides via level_backends and backend_overrides arguments to run_glm_pipeline()

FSL/FLAME backend reliability

  • Fix: FSL L3 jobs now wait on the backend-specific L2 producer job. FSL L3 setup/run jobs now depend on setup_run_l2_fsl when they consume FSL L2 outputs, avoiding races where L3 setup could start before the FSL L2 cache and FEAT outputs were ready.

  • Improved slice-parallel FLAME1+2 recovery. The local flame_runner keeps FSL’s default z-slice FLAME parallelization, but no longer fails the full model immediately when one FLAME12 slice crashes. Failed --runmode=flame12 slice commands are retried as --runmode=flame1, with FLAME12-only MCMC options removed from the retry command.

  • Surfaced FLAME12 slice fallbacks in logs. When a slice is recovered by FLAME1, the failed FLAME12 slice log directory is moved aside as statsNNNN.flame12_failed.*, and the FEAT directory receives a flame_runner_fallbacks.tsv audit file. These records are also promoted into the level-specific lgr model-estimation logs (logs/l1_estimation.*, logs/l2_estimation.*, or logs/l3_estimation.*) as warnings so users can see that estimation recovered by falling back to FLAME1 for one or more slices.

Level 1 setup refactor

  • Refactor setup_l1_models into smaller helper functions (setup_l1_subject, load_cached_l1_bdm, drop_runs_without_events)
  • Improved build_design_matrix error messages for missing onset/duration columns and empty event tables

Other improvements

  • Support for SPM-style concatenated run handling at Level 1
  • AFNI 3dLMEr Level 3 execution backend with automatic -qVars detection and dataTable.txt generation
  • Backend specification defaults (default_glm_backend_specs) for FSL, SPM, and AFNI
  • lookup_feat_outputs() now returns stable, level-specific $l1, $l2, and $l3 tables by default, with an explicit format = "long" option. L2 passthroughs are represented as logical L2 rows and identify their L1 materialization and source image.

fmri.pipeline 0.2-1

  • Fix to use run_data$tr inside build_design_matrix call
  • Always include evt_time 0 in event-aligned outputs for MEDuSA
  • Provide time_audit argument in event alignment to output additional columns pertaining to alignment timing
  • include volume as column in outputs of voxelwise_deconvolution to support time audits
